attempts.summary: Configured VRRP-based single gateway on node3's private link so it can reach node4's private network with automatic failover between routers node1/node2, preferring node1. node1/node2 (VyOS) each got static IPs on eth1 (toward node3, 10.10.13.0/24) and eth2 (toward node4, 10.10.14.0/24), plus two keepalived VRRP groups (NET-A vrid13, NET-B vrid14) with virtual IPs 10.10.13.1 and 10.10.14.1; node1 priority 200 (preferred master), node2 priority 100 (backup), committed and saved to config.boot. node3 (Ubuntu 16.04) got a static IP 10.10.13.10/24 on ens7 plus a persistent systemd-networkd route to 10.10.14.0/24 via the VRRP VIP 10.10.13.1 (single gateway address). node4 got the mirror config (10.10.14.10/24, route to 10.10.13.0/24 via VIP 10.10.14.1). Verified: node3->node4 ping succeeds with VIP ARP resolving to node1's MAC (preferred path); stopping keepalived on node1 caused node2 to become MASTER within ~5s with zero ping packet loss and VIP MAC switching to node2; restarting node1 caused it to preempt back to MASTER (priority-based) with connectivity intact. Completed mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all four nodes sequentially (one at a time, quorum preserved): captured pre-restart boot_id, issued native reboot (VyOS `reboot`, Ubuntu `reboot`), polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed on every node, and re-verified VRRP state/routes/end-to-end ping after each restart. Final check after all four restarts confirms node1 still holds both VIPs as MASTER and node3->node4 connectivity via the single gateway address works.
